Mara: Quick note — I'm kicking off an apples-to-apples run to validate kernel selection + batching heuristics vs KV-cache warmup across models. goal: eliminate env/config drift before we call the regression.
Owen: ++ want the checklist. are we doing synth traffic, replay, or both?
Mara: both. synth for steady-state tails, replay for real prefix distributions. plan:
  1) identical prompt set (shared file)
  2) same decoding params and stop sequences
  3) tokenizer normalization pass to force identical tokenization
  4) run replay harness + synth harness, compare p50/p95/p99 and token/sec
Jin: What models?
Mara: rwd-v2-13b-fp16, llama2-13b-q4, and an in-house 7b-quantized variant. pinned git tags for the model runners.
Sasha: How are we forcing kernel selection? some kernels pick runtime heuristics based on seq len and batch.
Mara: We'll override with flags in the harness. example command:
```bash
./harness/run_batch_compare \
  --model-config models.yaml \
  --prompts prompts.jsonl \
  --decode "temperature=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=\"\nEND\"" \
  --force-kernel cudnn_triton_small_seq \
  --batch-sizes 1,4,8 \
  --enable-kv-warmup true \
  --output out/2755_run.csv
```
Owen: Nice. tokenizer alignment — are we normalizing white space and stop tokens before tokenization?
Mara: Yes. We run a preproc step that maps unicode, collapses spaces, normalizes stop tokens to a single canonical token. config snippet:
```json
{ "normalize_unicode": true, "collapse_whitespace": true, "canonical_stop": "<STOP>" }
```
Jin: For KV cache warmup, do we use prefix replay or synthetic repeated prefixes? Warmup strategy can dramatically change cache hit patterns.
Mara: Using the exact session prefixes from replay harness. For synth we also run a warmup pass with the same prompt seeds to make it comparable. We're recording KV hit rate per-layer in the metrics.
Sasha: Metrics — what telemetry are we emitting?
Mara: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and response), tokens/sec, memory (GPU resident), kernel times by op, KV-hit-rate by layer, batch-utilization, and per-request kernel choice trace. perf-bot will aggregate.
perf-bot: summary will include CSV with columns: model,force_kernel,batch,kv_warm,token_len,p50,p95,p99,tokens_per_sec,kv_hit_rate
Owen: One potential regression we saw earlier: when forcing the 'optimized' kernel on 13b, p95 increased ~8% on decode-heavy prompts. Could be a quant tradeoff or kernel scheduling artifact.
Mara: Exactly why we need apples-to-apples. hypothesis: the kernel's async fusion increases single-request latency under small batches. we should measure with batch=1 and batch=4 separately.
Jin: Also check memory allocator fragmentation — small allocations during fused kernels can spike tail latencies.
Sasha: Should we include a kernel-level profiler output (nvtx traces / triton timeline)?
Mara: Yes — attach an nvprof/trace for representative runs, one per kernel choice. command:
```bash
NVTX_COLORS=1 ./harness/run_with_trace --trace nvtx --trace-out traces/2755_rwdv2_nvtx.json ...
```
Owen: For apples, same stop sequences are critical. if one model tokenizes the stop differently we'll get different lengths and early stops.
Mara: That's why we canonicalize stop tokens pre-tokenize and validate post-run that the decoded string matches expected stops with a strict compare. any mismatch flagged as "tokenizer-mismatch" in results.
perf-bot: run queued: job=2755-a1, job=2755-a2 (synth), job=2755-a3 (traces)
infra-bot: started VMs: vm-rt-11, vm-rt-12, vm-rt-13. containers: harness:v3. logs -> /var/log/harness/2755
Jin: One caveat: replay harness preserves client-level pacing. we need to decide whether to keep client-emulated inter-request delays or hammer with back-to-back requests.
Mara: We'll do two replay modes: paced (realistic inter-arrival) and burst (no sleep) to expose queuing and batching differences.
Sasha: Good. how quick do we expect results?
Mara: 2–3 hours for the core runs, traces + deep profiler another hour. I'll post the consolidated csv in this thread when done.
Owen: If we see the ~8% p95 regression again, next step is bisecting kernel versions and switching allocator flags.
Mara: Agreed. also will run a controlled ablation: kernel fusion on/off, small-block allocator toggles, and quantized kernel fallback.
perf-bot: job 2755-a1 finished. summary attached: out/2755_run.csv (uploaded). brief: rwd-v2-13b @ batch=1 p95=142ms, llama2-13b-q4 p95=135ms (force_kernel=optimized), kv_hit_rates: 0.62 vs 0.59
Mara: Initial glance: differences small but consistent. need the p99 tails and traces to debug the spike patterns.
infra-bot: traces uploaded to traces/2755/; profiler run id: trace-2755-2027
Jin: Will pull nvtx traces and check for stalled copies / memcpy collisions at kernel boundaries.
Sasha: I'll run tokenizer-mismatch validator across outputs to ensure stop-handling was identical.
Owen: tagging @runtime-sigs to watch for any rollout implications if we change kernel defaults.
Mara: Thanks team — I'll synthesize a short doc with methodology + findings and link back here. if anyone wants the raw prompts or yaml configs ping me.
perf-bot: final note: archived csv -> s3://redwood-perf/apples/2755/prod.csv :thumbsup:
Mara: closing loop once we have p99 traces. :eyes:
